title: [Performance]: optimize DeepSeek V4 TurboQuant framework path
body:
Share DSV4 transform tensors and cache KV plans, fuse scale correction and cache
  packing, and align DSpark context KV rotation and compressed attention metadata. Restore the historical DSV4
  Hadamard sequence while preserving the SFA baseline path and standard CANN operator integration.

  Add regression coverage for transform compatibility, cache planning, context rotation, and NPU finalize behavior.

  ### What this PR does / why we need it?

  ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

  ### How was this patch tested?

• ### What this PR does / why we need it?

  Optimize the DeepSeek V4 TurboQuant path to reduce repeated allocations and kernel launches, and keep DSpark
  attention inputs consistent.

  • Share read-only transform tensors, centroids, and norm lookup tables across DSV4 layers; cache contiguous inverse
    transforms and TQ KV execution plans.

  • Fuse norm reduction, scale correction, and compact KV cache packing into one Triton kernel.
  • Rotate DSpark context KV into the same basis as queries and prevent compressed TQ layers from using SWA-only
    drafting metadata.

  • Restore the historical DSV4 Hadamard sign sequence for compatibility with the previously validated
    implementation.

  • Preserve the SFA baseline path and standard CANN TorchAPI/ACLNN integration.

  ### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

  No new configuration options or public API changes.

  DSV4 TurboQuant uses the historical rotation sequence and corrected DSpark context handling, which may change
  generated outputs compared with the current baseline. Non-TQ paths, including C8 and A5 quantization modes 1/2,
  retain their existing logic.

  ### How was this patch tested?

  • 189 related unit tests passed, covering TurboQuant, DSA attention, and DSpark context handling.
  • 8 NPU finalize regression tests passed, covering packed codes, scale correction, empty inputs, graph replay, and
    compilation reuse across row counts.

  • On NPU, compared against the historical implementation using the same TurboQuant operator: transforms, centroids,
    norm lookup tables, and forward/inverse/compression results matched exactly for 1, 17, and 257 rows.

  • Service smoke tests passed for short prompts, multi-turn chat, streaming, and two concurrent requests before the
    final Hadamard compatibility change.

  • Applicable pre-commit checks passed. actionlint was skipped due to an environment bootstrap issue; no workflow
    files changed.

  Long-context validation with the installed CANN 9.2 operator package exposed numerical failures; the same
  independent attention cases passed with the previously validated OPP binaries. No framework workaround was
  introduced. Full service validation after the final Hadamard change and A5 hardware validation remain pending.
